meghiya.notes: AN 9.3 and Ud 4.1 tell the attendant’s mango-grove episode. The page citation also picks up AN 9.2, whose questioner is unnamed.

metteyya.notes: DPPN distinguishes Tissa’s friend, the elder who asks about celibacy in Snp 4.7, from Bāvarī’s student, the young brahmin of Snp 5.3 (see DPPN under Tissa, nos. 8 and 9). The latter has no candidate here. The chapter summary at Snp 4.16:22.3 names Snp 4.7 in sequence.

migapathaka.notes: SN 41.1:2.1 places Citta at Migapathaka. The page citation also picks up SN 40.11, a discourse about godlings.

migasālā.notes: Migasālā asks Ānanda about her father Purāṇa and her uncle Isidatta in AN 6.44 and AN 10.75. AN 6.43 and AN 10.74 are adjacent page matches.

migāra.notes: AN 7.7 names the wealthy Migāra Rohaṇeyya. AN 7.8 and AN 7.9 discuss fetters. DPD’s MN 107 example refers to the longhouse of Migāra’s mother and supplies no identification with Rohaṇeyya.

migāramātupāsāda.notes: AN 3.66 and SN 3.11 name the longhouse. AN 3.65 and SN 3.10 are adjacent page matches.

missakā.notes: DN 20:17.6 has missakā ca yasassino in the gathering of deities. Sujato translates this as “and assorted glorious ones”, so the English name filter misses the group.

mithilā.notes: DN 19 names the Videhas’ city. The Maghadeva and Brahmāyu episodes are in MN 83 and MN 91 respectively. MN 82 and MN 90 are adjacent page matches.

moggalla.notes: AN 4.187:4.4 names Moggalla among King Eḷeyya’s men devoted to Rāmaputta. The citation lands in AN 4.191 and AN 4.192. The mention list also picks up the vocative moggallāna addressed to Mahāmoggallāna, for example in AN 4.167 and AN 4.168.

moliyasīvaka.notes: AN 6.47 and SN 36.21 name the wanderer. The adjacent AN 6.46 concerns Mahācunda.

mucalinda.notes: Ud 2.1:1.2 places the Buddha at the foot of the Mucalinda tree (mucalindamūle). The two tappable mucalindo forms identify the dragon king. Mucalinda 02 is the entry for the tree, and the packet has no entry headed by the king. A tree identification on those taps would be misleading. DN 8 supplies no evidence for the Himalayan lake in Mucalinda 04.

muttā.notes: AN 8.91–117 lists the lay disciple Muttā. AN 8.89 and AN 8.90 concern monastic procedures. The packet lacks entries for the trainee addressed by the Buddha in Thig 1.2 and the elder who sings of freedom from the mortar, pestle, and husband in Thig 1.11.

māhissati.notes: The packet finds the city on the students’ route in Snp 5.1. DN 19:36.5 also names the Avantis’ city, with the variant Mahesayaṁ in the Pali and Māhissatī in Sujato.

mānadinna.notes: SN 47.30 recounts Ānanda’s visit to the sick householder. SN 47.31 is an adjacent page match.

mānatthaddha.notes: The packet misses the brahmin in SN 7.15:1.2 (mānatthaddho nāma brāhmaṇo), whose name Sujato translates as “Stuck-Up”. SN 7.14 concerns a different brahmin. The list of privately awakened Buddhas is in MN 116, with MN 117 picked up on the same page.

mātaṅga.notes: MN 116 lists the privately awakened Buddha. MN 56:13.27 names the forest in the compound mātaṅgāraññaṁ. Snp 1.7:25–28 tells of the corpse-worker’s son Mātaṅga, who reaches the Brahmā realm. The packet lacks entries for the forest and for that man.

māṇavagāmiya.notes: SN 2.30 names the godling among the visitors and attributes his verse to him. SN 2.29 concerns Susīma.

nagaravinda.notes: MN 150 places the Buddha in this Kosalan brahmin village. The adjacent MN 149 opens at Sāvatthī.

nala.notes: DN 32:10.9 and 12.258 read naḷo rājā janesabho. Sujato spells the name Nala, which the English filter misses. DN 20:10.10 has the same pair of kings, with naḷorājā joined and given its own dictionary line.

nalakapāna.notes: MN 68 and AN 10.67–68 place the grove at Naḷakapāna. The neighboring citations lead to Cātumā in MN 67 and the Magadhan village of Nālaka in AN 10.66.

nanda.notes: AN 6.57, MN 36, and MN 76 name Nanda Vaccha, for whom the packet has no entry. AN 7.53 names a laywoman’s son, also absent. AN 1.240 (in AN 1.235–247), DN 16, and SN 55.8 name nuns called Nandā. Thag 1.36 gives Nanda 19’s name as Kumāputta, which explains its absence from the allowed list. Ud 1.5 names a senior monk without distinguishing him further. The page matches AN 1.248–257, AN 8.8, SN 21.9, SN 35.242, and SN 2.26 do not identify the respective Nandas. Ud 3.2:10.2 promises Nanda five hundred nymphs, where Nanda 01 describes a promise of one wife.
